topic: Lambda Design: Syntactic Sugar for Manual Closure Classes
explanation: Lambda expressions are purely syntactic sugar, instructing the compiler to synthesize an anonymous closure type. This generated class encapsulates captured external variables as private data members and implements the lambda body within its overloaded function call operator (`operator()`). The expression evaluates to an instance of this closure type, known as the closure object. This design confirms that lambdas are not primitive language features; their functionality is entirely reproducible by manually defining the equivalent closure class. This manual replication is sometimes necessary to implement advanced capture semantics, such as the C++11 workaround for move capture prior to the introduction of C++14 init capture.
practical_example: When working in a codebase restricted to C++11, a developer needs to capture a `std::unique_ptr` into a function object. Knowing the lambda's underlying implementation allows them to bypass the C++11 language limitation by manually creating the closure class to handle the required move semantics.
chapter: Item 32: Use init capture to move objects into closures
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
